summary: Lets a refreshed activity-bridge result be recorded while an onboarding batch is in preflight (only through onboarding_record_bridge, on the current snapshot), so ordinary new Trusted activity no longer strands a batch after a PASS preflight. The stage does not move; the preflight is rebuilt and re-approved. No rows change.

preflight.name: onboarding_record_bridge exists (484)
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'onboarding_record_bridge'

preflight.name: onboarding_stage_events_validate exists (481/485)
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'onboarding_stage_events_validate'

expected_changes: Replaces onboarding_record_completion: an activity_bridge result may be recorded while the batch is in preflight only when the bridge writer is on (onboarding_record_bridge); every other stage result still needs its own stage.
Replaces onboarding_record_bridge: allowed in activity_bridge or preflight; the current-snapshot, sha and fingerprint rules are unchanged.

Replaces onboarding_stage_events_validate (485 body): the same exception for a stage_completed activity_bridge event under the bridge writer; waivers, advances and approvals still require their own stage.
No onboarding, batch or accounting rows change.

verify.name: onboarding_record_bridge now admits the preflight stage
verify.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'onboarding_record_bridge' AND prosrc LIKE '%NOT IN (''activity_bridge'', ''preflight'')%'

verify.name: the validate trigger carries the bridge-writer exception
verify.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'onboarding_stage_events_validate' AND prosrc LIKE '%onboarding.bridge_writer%'
